newsitem.title: USA: US natgas utilities invest in firm to make loans.
newsitem.headline: US natgas utilities invest in firm to make loans.

text.p: More than a dozen natural gas utilities have invested in a new company that will use capital from the Federal National Mortgage Association to make loans for energy-efficiency home improvements, the American Gas Association said Monday.
The AGA's board of directors last month authorized the new company, called the American Gas Finance Co or "GasFinCo".
Owners of existing one-to four-family dwellings will be eligible for GasFinCo loans of up to $15,000, and can take up to 10 years to repay the unsecured loan.

The loans could finance installation of natural gas heating systems and water heaters, and could be used to finance more energy-efficient appliances, a homeowner's share of extending a gas main to the house, or the cost of removing an oil tank when switching a heating system to natural gas, the AGA said.
With the plan, the contractor is paid by the utility or by GasFinCo, and the right to receive the customer's loan payments, including interest, in then transferred to GasFinCo.
The utility can bill the customer directly, or let GasFinCo do so, the AGA said.
